transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because things just don’t feel like mine anymore, if that makes sense. I used to get excited about stuff—murals, going for runs, basketball, even making a really good drink at work. Lately I just kind of stand there like I don’t care about any of it. It’s probably not the biggest thing, but… it’s been bothering me.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About two months, I think. It kind of started after the bar got bought out and… all the stuff I’d been working toward there just changed. I mean, maybe I’m making too much of it, but that’s when I noticed it.
Do you still enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable, or has the pleasure gone away?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say I still do, but not really. The pleasure’s kind of gone flat. Stuff I used to get into—painting murals, going for a run, playing basketball, even making a drink just right at work—I mostly just… stand there. Like I know I should care, but I don’t feel much from it. Is that what you mean?
Have you been having any thoughts about hurting yourself or wishing you were dead?

I… I don’t know. I don’t think so? I mean, I’ve had some pretty low moments, but I wouldn’t want you to think I’m, like, going to do something. It’s more just… feeling worn down, I guess. Is that an okay way to put it?
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?
A little, maybe… I mean, I wouldn’t call it anxiety exactly. I’ve just been kind of uneasy sometimes, like I can’t quite settle. But it’s probably not that big of a thing. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Maybe a little, yeah. I haven’t really been keeping track, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. It’s more that I’m not eating right. Most days I’ll get through my shift and forget to eat until my hands start shaking behind the bar, and then after closing I’ll grab a few bites of something cold… but even looking at it kind of makes me feel sick. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling like you're moving more slowly than usual?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed myself moving slower… maybe I’m a little tired sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s enough to call it that. Do I seem slow to you?
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m feeling sorry for myself or anything. But I do keep thinking I let people down. The younger bartenders, and some artists I’d promised space to… it feels like I wrecked their shot somehow.

And then I get this thought that maybe I deserve whatever happens to me because of it. I know that probably sounds… dramatic. Is that the kind of guilt you mean?
Would you say that these feelings of not caring and being worn down are present most of the day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s kind of why I came in. Most of the day it feels like nothing really… belongs to me anymore, if that makes sense.

I used to get excited about murals, going for runs, playing basketball, even just making a really good drink for somebody. Now I’ll be standing there doing it and it’s like I’m watching someone else’s hands. I just don’t care the way I used to. Is that what you mean?
Would you say these feelings of not caring and being worn down are interfering with your ability to work or take care of things at home?

Yeah… I guess it is. I mean, I’m still trying to keep up, I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve just stopped functioning or anything. But I’ve missed several shifts, and when I am there I’ve made closing mistakes I never used to make.

That’s embarrassing to say. People used to trust me to handle things, and now my coworkers are kind of double-checking my work. At home or outside work… I’ve stopped showing up for runs, basketball, mural shoots with friends. I tell myself I’ll go, and then I just… can’t make myself get there. Is that what you mean by interfering?
Would you say these feelings of not caring and being worn down have been present every day for the past two months?

Yeah… pretty much every day, I think. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m counting it exactly, but it’s been about two months.

It kind of started after the bar got bought out and everything I’d been working toward just… changed. Since then it’s been there most days, honestly. Does that answer it right?
Would you say that your feelings of not caring and being worn down are severe enough that they're nearly constant and really interfering with your daily life?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, “nearly constant” sounds strong, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been getting in the way pretty clearly.

I’ve missed several shifts, and when I do go in I’ve made closing mistakes I never used to make. People used to just trust me with that stuff, and now coworkers are double-checking me, which… yeah, that’s hard to admit.

And outside work I’ve kind of stopped showing up for things with friends — runs, basketball, mural shoots. I tell myself I’m going to go, and then I just can’t make myself get there. So… yes, I guess it is interfering with daily life. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you're resting or sleeping more than usual?

Not more, no… if anything I’m not sleeping right. I’ll lie down exhausted, like I should just pass out, but my head keeps going over every mistake I made at work.

Then when I finally do fall asleep, I’m waking up around four or five, and I can’t really get back down after that. I mean, I’m still getting some sleep, so I don’t want to overstate it, but it hasn’t been restful. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety lately?

I don’t think so… not in the way I picture, like pacing around or tapping all the time.

I mean, I might shift around a bit when I’m uncomfortable, but I haven’t really noticed being especially fidgety or restless lately. Unless you mean something more subtle?
Do you feel like you're having trouble concentrating or making decisions lately?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function at all, but it’s definitely not like me.

At work, inventory used to be automatic — I’d just go down the bottles and know what needed counting. Lately I’ll just kind of stare at them and lose count two or three times. Or I’ll freeze on something stupidly simple, like deciding which garnish to restock first.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. But yes, I guess concentration and decisions have been harder. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that there are any times during the day when you feel somewhat better, or is the feeling of being worn down consistent throughout the day?

It’s… pretty consistent, I think. I don’t know that there’s a time where I suddenly feel normal.

Maybe I can push through better once I’m moving, but even then, by the time I carry a couple cases of liquor or set up the well, my body feels like I’ve already worked a double — even if I barely did anything earlier that day.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but yeah, worn down is probably the right word.
Would you say that these feelings of being worn down and not caring are so bad that they're affecting almost every aspect of your life?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to say “every aspect” if that sounds too big, but… it’s gotten into a lot of things.

Work especially. I’ve missed several shifts, which I really don’t like admitting. And I’ve made closing mistakes I never used to make — little things that should be automatic. Now people have to double-check my work, and that’s… hard, because I used to be someone they could just trust to handle it.

And outside work, I’ve kind of stopped showing up for things. Friends ask about runs, or basketball, or going out to shoot murals, and I just… can’t seem to make myself go. I usually tell them I’m tired or busy.

So yes, I guess it is affecting more than I’d like. Is that what you mean?
Would you say that there are any activities or things that you still enjoy or look forward to, even if it's just a little bit?

I wish I could say yes. I mean… maybe there are little moments, but they don’t really last.

That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. It feels like nothing feels like mine anymore. I used to get excited about going out to photograph murals, going for runs, playing basketball… even making a really good drink at work, getting it just right. Now I’m mostly just standing there like… I don’t care about any of it.

I don’t like saying that, because it sounds bad. But no, I’m not really looking forward to much lately. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
Would you say that your feelings of not caring and being worn down are so severe that they completely dominate your daily life?

I don’t know if I’d say “completely,” because I can still get myself through parts of the day sometimes. But… yeah, it’s dominating more than I want to admit.

I’ve missed several shifts, and when I do make it in, I’ve made closing mistakes I never used to make. Now coworkers are double-checking things that people used to just trust me with, which feels pretty awful.

And outside of work, I’ve stopped showing up for friends — runs, basketball, going out to shoot murals. I keep saying I’m tired or busy, but really I just can’t make myself go.

So… I guess yes, it’s taken over a lot of my daily life. Is that the kind of answer you mean?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent feelings of not caring, loss of pleasure in activities, changes in appetite, sleep disturbances, fatigue, feelings of guilt, and difficulty concentrating are consistent with a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder, which is further specified as having a moderate severity given the impact on daily functioning and the presence of these symptoms for over two months.
